title: The property tracks of AnimationPlayer will disrupt the animation transition functionality.
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4] ### System information Godot v4.6.3.stable - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 29 Jun 2026 21:45:42 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (CFL GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.46 GiB memory ### Issue description run1: run2: code: Ideally, the `run1` animation would use a property track to set the `walking` variable to `true` at the start, then automatically transition to the `run2` animation upon completion. The `run2` animation would then set the `walking` variable to `false` at its end. In fact, there is a probability that the `run1` animation may not transition correctly to the `run2` animation at the end, which is more likely to occur at low frame rates (this can be simulated by using a higher running speed or setting the `callback_mode_process` of the `AnimationPlayer` to `physics`). To avoid this issue, the variable `walking` must be manually set to `true` while playing `run1`. bug： https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19f26f60-fb56-44bf-aa66-93906341bbf9 In fact, there is a probability that the `run1` animation may not transition correctly to the `run2` animation at the end, which is more likely to occur at low frame rates (this can be simulated by using a higher running speed or setting the `callback_mode_process` of the `AnimationPlayer` to `physics`). To avoid this issue, the variable `walking` must be manually set to `true` while playing `run1`. ### Steps to reproduce Using high-speed MPR, observe the impact of `walking = true` on the animation in the code. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [animationtest_2026-07-03_17-36-04.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29630103/animationtest_2026-07-03_17-36-04.zip)
